findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed prep cooler next to salad dispenser to be cold holding at 52F. Discussed with PIC, inspector will follow up on cooler on October 14, 2026. TCS items within cooler were prepared and put in cooler 2 hours before facility opened. TCS items were moved to other working cooler units. Ensure any TCS food being cold held is kept at or below 41F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.

findings.comment: Observed handle of salad tong to be resting in contact with salad within cooler. Discussed with PIC, tong was relocated to a plate near salad cooler. Ensure only food contact surfaces of utensils are in contact with food.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.11 Food Contact with Equipment and Utensils. findings.comment:
Observed a container of soup to be hot holding at 129F. Discussed with PIC, soup was moved to stove and reheated to 165F. Ensure any TCS food being hot held is kept at or above 135F. 

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

1) The triple sink near the dish machine hand sink. 
2) The dish machine hand sink.
3) The back kitchen hand sink.
4) The mop/dump sink.

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

An employee was observed to wash their hands and use their bare hand to turn off the faucet, recontaminating the hands. They then proceeded to handle plates of RTE foods while touching the food contact side of the plate. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to ensure that proper hand washing is taking place in the facility at al times.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-801.11: (D) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact READY-TO-EAT FOOD as specified under  3-301.11(B) and (E). 

A dixie cup is observed stored in the Italian beef on the steam table. The PIC was shown and removed the cup to correct the immediate concern. A similar violation was noted on the previous routine inspection at the salad station, making this a repeat situation. Use appropriate utensils while handling RTE foods to prevent bare hand contact of the foods.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple nozzles of the fountain drink machines are observed soiled during this inspection. To a lesser extent the soda gun in the bar area was also soiled. The PIC indicated that they were cleaned a couple times a week. This seems to be insufficient for the facility’s current use. The nozzles were removed and cleaned during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that they are cleaned often enough to be maintained in a clean state.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C).

Two large tubs of ground beef in the walk in cooler are without date marking. The PIC indicated that they were made yesterday and the day before. Stickers were added to the tubs to correct the violation. Ensure that all RTE TCS foods are labeled with the date that they have their package opened or are cooked.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. 

Two syrup bottles in the standing cooler to the right of the pizza prep station are observed with mold growth on the outside of the containers. The PIC was shown and the items discarded during this inspection to correct. Ensure that the containers for RTE items are maintained clean at all times.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. 

Multiple moist rags in the kitchen are observed on the counters. The PIC was consulted and instructed to maintain the in-use rags in sanitizer solution between uses. The rags were moved during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

On arrival, there was not a sani bucket prepared in the kitchen area. Food handling and preparation activities were observed throughout the kitchen. When discussed with the PIC a bucket was produced to correct the violation. Ensure that there is an in-use sanitizer available at all times that food handling/preparation is taking place.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Allergen training is only available for 3 of the CFPMs during this inspection. Per previous notes the facility has information about taking/retaking the certification. Ensure that all CFPMs have completed allergen training prior to the next routine inspection.
